faq.q: Why cut the circle into slices?
faq.a: Slices can be rearranged into a shape we already know, a rectangle. The thinner the slices, the closer it gets to a perfect rectangle.
asks: How do you prove the area of a circle?

faq.q: Why is the rectangle pi r long?
faq.a: Half the slices' crust is along the top and half along the bottom. The whole crust is 2 pi r, so each long side is half of that: pi r.
asks: Why is the length half the circumference?

faq.q: What is the formula for the area of a circle?
faq.a: Area equals pi times the radius times the radius, written pi r squared.

faq.q: Why does doubling the radius make 4 times the area?
faq.a: The radius is used twice in pi r squared. Doubling it doubles both, so the area grows 2 times 2, which is 4 times.
asks: Is a 20 cm pizza twice a 10 cm pizza?

faq.q: What is the area of a circle with radius 3 cm?
faq.a: Pi times 3 times 3 is about 3.14 times 9, which is about 28.3 square centimetres.

facts: Area of a circle = πr², where r is the radius.
A circle of radius 10 cm has an area of about 314 cm²; radius 20 cm gives about 1,256 cm².

quiz.say: What is the area of a circle with radius 10 centimetres? Use pi as 3.14.
A circle has a diameter of 6 centimetres. What radius do you use in pi r squared?
quiz.why: The radius is half the diameter, so 3 centimetres.

wrong.1: 6 is the diameter, a common mistake.
